decisions.reason: The continuous formulation permits bounded Lipschitz domains; the discrete clause separately assumes a finite conforming triangular mesh using the cited exact affine mesh convention. Such a mesh covers the domain closure by finitely many straight triangles and requires the domain to be their union's interior, hence it is polyhedral. Nonpolyhedral domains admit no such mesh and are not discrete instances. The definition makes no mesh-existence assertion, so the RT supplier's domain hypothesis is satisfied whenever X_h is invoked.

The DPG definition concerns global skeleton ranges, whereas the local quotient on an arbitrary open set is supplied exactly by lem-na-hdiv-weak-normal-trace. The opening attribution was inaccurate but the proof already cites the correct local supplier as F4. Replaced that attribution without changing the quotient, Green functional, scope, onto conclusion or lift bound. Checked H1 completeness by L2 convergence, Riesz for L composed with q, the sign div(grad z)=z, and the resulting graph-norm bound, including the empty domain and zero functional.

The rectangular spectral condition number used by the cited theorem is sigma_1/sigma_n and requires n>=1. A zero-column matrix has rank zero (full column rank) but no extremal singular values, so the original unconditional matrix sentence applied F2 outside its domain. Added m>=n>=1 in the Statement, Given and F2 and used both size and rank in step 2.1. The exact-arithmetic caveat remains unchanged; the conditioning identity follows from the squared positive singular values of A^T A.

The four volume fields are independent on a nondegenerate triangle, while the constant vector/scalar test space has dimension three. Its positive Gram matrix makes the practical map linear, so rank-nullity supplies a nonzero kernel and nonuniqueness of every consistent normal system. The title was broader than the stated concrete counterexample; narrowed only the title to the smaller constant-test example. Statement and proof remain unchanged.

F4 attributed orthogonal projections to a Riesz statement that supplies only representatives and their norm equality. Corrected F4 to that exact interface. This is nonfatal because step 1.1 already constructs epsilon_h in an orthonormal basis, so orthogonality and Pythagoras follow directly. Checked restriction efficiency, Fortin cancellation in the delta estimate, the zero-delta case, oscillation's best-approximation bound, and mean-preserving cellwise h-weighted Poisson oscillation. All theorem clauses remain unchanged.

The ideal Poisson algorithm requires its particular ultraweak spaces and bilinear form, so it is not an applicable supplier for the R2 matrix model. This citation/interface defect is nonfatal: the already-listed finite-dimensional Riesz theorem licenses the representatives and direct arithmetic establishes every claimed value. Defined both model maps explicitly in F1/F2 using that theorem, checked their representing equations for all admissible test vectors, and retained the Poisson algorithms only as analogies in Remarks. Ae2=(1,1), restricted test=e1, and the positive scalar equations give the unique coefficients 1/2 and 1.
